source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 16 January 1924, p. 7 ("Belfast municipal elections: the results"); Belfast News-Letter, 7 January 1924, p. 7 ("List of nominations: many Labour candidates in the field")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: candidates, labels, electorate, valid votes and majority from the News-Letter's ward-by-ward results (INA OCR); * = retiring member as printed; where the OCR of a vote is garbled the figure used is the one that agrees with both the printed valid votes and the printed majority; full names from the nomination list

note: Annual election of one councillor in each of the 15 wards of Belfast Corporation (the member retiring in rotation), nominations Saturday 5 January, poll Tuesday 15 January 1924. Ten wards were contested; Falls, St Anne's, Shankill, Smithfield and Windsor returned their members unopposed (Belfast News-Letter, 7 and 16 January 1924). Labour gained Court and Dock, and an Independent Unionist St George's. Smylie replaced the retiring member. The printed majority is illegible in the OCR.
correctionNote: The PRONI register staging (Nov 2026) changed Hugh Smylie's vote to 3,322, as the Belfast Corporation register of members (PRONI LA/7/1/CA/1/3) records it. It is restored to the printed 3,332 (proni-items and council-audit, Nov 2026), read on the page image of the Belfast News-Letter, 16 January 1924, p. 7: the paper's majority of 963 and its 5,701 valid votes both require 3,332 (34 spoiled papers), so the register's 3,322 is a slip of the pen.
